title: Ensemble quantization profile & stability tests for embedding models (INT8/FP16)
creator: Priya Shah
description: Problem: When serving embeddings with INT8 or mixed FP16/INT8 profiles we occasionally observe dataset-specific similarity regressions after model compilation and kernel selection. This ticket defines an ensemble-style calibration workflow, a holdout-based validation harness, and a monitoring playbook to detect and mitigate cosine-similarity drift without excessive nightly re-calibration. Goal: produce a reproducible pipeline that outputs a small set (1-3) of vetted quantization profiles per model + HW target, automated validation against holdout corpora, and an ops-friendly alerting threshold definition for production runs.
acceptance_criteria: Produce an automated calibration pipeline that generates at most 3 candidate quant profiles per model/hardware target
Define a holdout validation dataset per customer-vertical and per-language family and run nightly drift checks
Validation harness reports: median cosine delta, 95th percentile regression, and percent-of-queries below similarity threshold
A rollout gating rule that prevents promoting a profile if 95th percentile cosine delta > 0.03 or median decrease > 0.01
Monitoring playbook created with concrete triage steps, rollback path, and a GitHub runbook link
calibration_workflow: Step 1 - Seed dataset selection: sample N=200k sentences across corpora buckets (docs, search, chat) with stratified sampling by length and language
Step 2 - Ensemble calibration: run three calibration strategies in parallel: per-layer min-max+scale, per-channel asymmetric, and weight-aware KL minimization
Step 3 - Profile distillation: collapse the three candidates to 1-3 profiles using a stability score (mean quant error + layer variance + latency penalty), store profile artifacts in S3
Step 4 - Binary packaging: create runtime-compatible profile bundles (profile.json + metadata) and upload to model-catalog for canary runs
Step 5 - Canary: deploy candidate profiles to 1% traffic on dedicated infra for 24h, collect embedding samples and token-level perf metrics
validation_plan: Holdout datasets: maintain per-model holdouts (enterprise docs, open-web, synthetic paraphrase sets). Each holdout has a baseline embedding set computed with full-precision reference.
Metrics to compute: cosine distribution shift, K-S distance on similarity CDFs, fraction of pairs that drop below application thresholds (e.g., 0.7 for near-duplicate detection)
Perturbation suite: add gaussian noise to inputs, random truncation, length scaling to check robustness of quant profiles
Acceptance gating: a profile passes validation if median cosine delta <= 0.01 AND 95th percentile delta <= 0.03 across all holdouts
Regression diagnostics: per-layer contribution report and per-bucket failure breakdown to aid mitigation (recalibrate layer, increase precision for top-K layers)
Automated report: generate a single-line verdict and a human-readable PDF summarizing the runs for the release notes
monitoring_playbook: Alert rules: trigger when daily median cosine delta > 0.015 OR 95th percentile delta > 0.035 across production sampling
Immediate triage: switch traffic to fallback profile (higher-precision variant) and open a P1 incident with on-call inference team
Data capture: persist failing example inputs, model version, profile id, hardware, and per-layer quant stats to a secure bucket for debugging
Postmortem steps: run the validation pipeline with full holdouts, produce layer-delta visualizations, and propose profile fixes or weight-aware remap
Rollout guidance: bump canary to 10% after fixes and monitor sliding-window metrics for 48 hours before wider promotion
risks: Calibration compute costs may spike if holdout sizes are large; we need budget limits and sampling heuristics
Overfitting calibration to synthetic corpora can miss customer-specific distributional shifts
Latency regressions if a profile increases kernel execution variance; must include latency penalty in stability score
False positives in alerts from A/B traffic noise—require smoothing and minimum sample counts
